name: RADES
summary: RADES increases the effective detection volume at high frequencies with coupled microwave-cavity arrays; CAST-RADES is an implemented phase.
detection_principle: Multiple small cavities form an electromagnetic-filter resonator that coherently receives axion-conversion signals in a strong field.

status.label: Multiphase project: completed experiments alongside further construction / design
status.evidence: Published 2025 high-field superconducting-cavity results coexist with the future BabyIAXO approach; they do not mean the full BabyIAXO instrument is operating.

timeline.event: First results of the CAST-RADES haloscope search for axions at 34.67 μeV

collaboration.name: RADES Collaboration / project team

phases.name: CAST-RADES
phases.description: Cavity-array search in the CAST magnet.

phases.name: RADES-BabyIAXO
phases.description: Planned low-frequency search using the BabyIAXO magnet.

results.summary: The 2021 result found no signal and set a coupling limit of approximately 4×10⁻¹³ GeV⁻¹ at 95% credibility.
The high-temperature-superconductor-coated cavity collected 27 h of data in CERN's 11.7 T magnet, finding no excess at 36.5676–36.5699 μeV.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
